To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the majority of women with B2 or B1 needle core biopsy diagnoses are not referred for surgery, that the risk of malignancy following B2 or B2 needle core biopsy diagnoses is 1.6% and 0.4% respectively, and that the risk of a false-negative biopsy diagnosis is 0.5% and 0% respectively.
The rate of malignancy after a benign (B2, B3) core needle biopsy diagnosis is 10-12%, and that the rate of malignancy following an initial benign diagnosis (B1) is 1.5-2%.

1) the rate of malignant lesions detected on core biopsy was 2.5%, 2) the rate of malignancy detected at excision was 4.3% (3.8% for B1 and 4.9% for B2 lesions), 3) the rate of invasive carcinoma was 1.8%, 4) 4.1% of the patients underwent mastectomy, 5) the rate of upgrade to invasive carcinoma was 3.1%,
In summary, our research is concerned with
the management of patients with breast cancer.
the management of screen-detected breast lesions following benign (B3) or normal (A1/A2/A3) needle core biopsy (NCB) diagnoses.
the development and evaluation of a novel method to predict breast cancer risk based on the use of mammographic texture analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a diagnosis of benign breast disease on a needle core biopsy does not rule out the possibility of breast cancer.
a B1 or B2 needle biopsy is not diagnostic of a benign breast disease and that a B3 diagnosis does not necessarily mean that the lesion is malignant.
a benign diagnosis on needle biopsy is not a reliable predictor of benign disease in the excision specimen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of patients diagnosed with breast cancer after a B1 or B2 biopsy have a favorable prognosis.
the use of the B2 category is not justified.

the majority of screen detected breast cancers diagnosed following a benign (B2), normal (B1), or inconclusive (B3) core biopsy diagnosis are invasive ductal carcinomas (IDC) of low grade, low stage, and low proliferative index.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of needle core biopsy for diagnosis of breast lesions has been associated with an increased risk of breast cancer.
the majority of women with a B2 diagnosis will be spared surgery, and that the majority of those who are operated on will have no evidence of cancer.
the use of a benign (B2), or even normal (B1), needle core biopsy diagnosis is associated with a significant risk for a subsequent diagnosis of cancer, and that this risk increases with age.
